name: Jorge Sampaoli
scopeNote: Counted: Universidad de Chile (15 Dec 2010 announced; left late Nov/early Dec 2012, exact day not found) and Chile national team (Dec 2012 to 19 Jan 2016, exact start day not found, Los Andes says diciembre de 2012). Style term used by sources: Bielsista / Bielsismo (3-4-3 and 3-1-4-2 at La U, 3-4-1-2 / 4-1-2-1-2 / 3-2-5 in possession with Chile, high press and counterpress, man-oriented marking by the back line). Spell-end 2016-01-19 comes from the FourFourTwo article date (terms of departure agreed). Excluded for this run, not researched: Sevilla 2016-17, Argentina 2017-18, Santos 2019, Atletico Mineiro 2020-21, Marseille 2021-22, Flamengo 2023 and earlier minor clubs. The statedView items dated after the counted period are kept because stated views are not period-limited.
openQuestions: Exact end of the Universidad de Chile spell and start of the Chile spell: a search summary (not read on a page) said ANFP announced him on 3 Dec 2012 and the Clinic dated a 22 Nov 2012 article about him leaving for Chile; 2012-12-02 and 2012-12-03 are placeholders from that, not verified.
Exact end date 2016-01-19: FourFourTwo dated 2016-01-19 says terms agreed; a search summary said he resigned on 19 Jan 2016. Confirm with a second page.

Sevilla 2016-17 and Argentina 2017-18 are real candidates for inclusion (recognisable style, move to bigger jobs); excluded here only for budget and because the brief's likely spells were Univ. de Chile and Chile. Atletico Mineiro, Santos, Marseille and Flamengo not examined; no titles or dates are claimed from memory.

Brief says 'three league titles'; read pages confirm Apertura 2011 win (Cooperativa), Apertura 2012 win (Cooperativa) and Copa Sudamericana December 2011; the Clausura 2011 title was not read on a page. Ballverliebt says the club was winning its third consecutive national title in 2012.
Sportskeeda says Sampaoli freed Medel to man-mark Messi in the final per a search summary; the page read does not state it, so it is not recorded.

The two statedView entries dated 2016-01-08 are the Cooperativa article date; the original Sábado interview and the book Leones have no date found. Spell-excluded entries have year-only dates because they were not researched. Set-pieces: no page read covers Sampaoli's set-piece design.

Sampaoli's 2019 and 2017 remarks (youth debuts, Vidal) are retrospective statements about the period; the 2016-04-22 FIFA interview is after the spell end, so its stated-view entry is verified:false and the view is kept in statedView[].
Spielverlagerung dates Chile-Bolivia article 2015-06-22; the match is only given as 2015-06 here because the digest does not give the match day.

sources.title: Spielverlagerung: Copa America Preview: Chile
sources.evidence: Sampaoli has used a 3-4-1-2 regularly with great success over the last couple of years however has employed a formation with two centre backs at times.

sources.title: Spielverlagerung: Copa America Preview: Chile
sources.evidence: Chile often adopt a 3-2-5 shape in possession, overloading an oppositions back four.

sources.title: Spielverlagerung: Copa America Preview: Chile
sources.evidence: Chile build up from very deep, drawing out the opposition. The centre-backs spread to the corners of the 18-yard area to make them more difficult to press as play is stretched over a wider area.

sources.title: Spielverlagerung: Copa America Preview: Chile
sources.evidence: Chile always try to stretch the opposition both laterally and vertically. They stretch the opposition laterally when they have the ball in the opposition’s half using the high and wide positioning of the fullbacks.

sources.title: Spielverlagerung: Copa America Preview: Chile
sources.evidence: Chile also consistently exercise elements of Juego de Posicion, with their own style often being referred to as ‘Posesion (Spanish) 74’.

sources.title: Spielverlagerung: Copa America Preview: Chile
sources.evidence: Chile set up a high press with the man on the ball almost always being pressed, usually by the ever-energetic Sanchez.

sources.title: Spielverlagerung: Copa America Preview: Chile
sources.evidence: Their back five allows them to man-mark men dropping to receive the ball from their defenders without leaving too much space in behind.

sources.title: Spielverlagerung: Copa America Preview: Chile
sources.evidence: Chile play a very compact pressing game and a high line to accompany it. However, when this press is breached for whatever reason this leaves them highly vulnerable.

sources.title: Spielverlagerung: Copa America Preview: Chile
sources.evidence: Chile do most of their defending in the opposition’s half and their aggressive pressing and counterpressing is what has made them such a footballing cult. They are always looking to win the ball instead of just dropping off

sources.title: Spielverlagerung: Copa America Preview: Chile
sources.evidence: Chile are also extremely fortunate that they have a goalkeeper who is very comfortable on the ball under pressure and is arguably the best ‘keeper at passing in the world.

sources.title: World Soccer: Tactics: winning ways with Universidad de Chile
sources.evidence: His basic model is a 3-4-3, with striker Eduardo Vargas (now with Napoli) cutting in from the right. Where Sampaoli stands out, though, is in his tweaks for individual games, which have been extraordinarily varied and highly effective.

sources.title: World Soccer: Tactics: winning ways with Universidad de Chile

When we took the job on, we tried to be as direct, aggressive and offensive as he was, though we had to try and bring in a bit of control. We started to defend a lot more with the ball, and that eventually gave the team the confidence to dictate every game and get on top of the opposition.
